# Rule 1 - Play your Character
## There are no main characters.
Be a believable, if not normal person that could reasonably be hired by NanoTrasen.
Keep OOC out of IC chats, and keep IC chats out of OOC while a round is going on. If teaching a new player, for example, use Help, or try your best to incorporate it into the roleplay.
Your character's life is important, value it. Avoid making decisions that no reasonable person would make. (Like trying to take on threats alone, or agreeing to be turned into food.)
Playstyles that disregard all opportunities for engagement and roleplay can be met with administrative action.
Stay in your lane regarding your role with the exception of emergencies and other extenuating circumstances. Security should not be performing surgery, and Medical should not be performing security duties. Though Crew should be the last line of defense if all other means fail. This applies to non-antagonists intentionally making Security's life harder for no roleplay reason whatsoever. This includes Thavens with a mood for worshiping animals, leading them to take over the Chapel.
## Have an Appropriate Name
If a name could reasonably appear on a driver's license in the year 2984, it's probably alright. The [textlink="naming scheme" link="NamingScheme"] is a guideline, as all species are allowed to have each other's naming conventions (ie. Vox being named like a Moth) as long as the name follows all other blanket rules EXCEPT for Greys, whose naming conventions cannot be used by other species nor take from another species themselves. All species can have a First and Last name like humanoids. Synthetic trait characters cannot have "IPC" or Silicon names. Names may contain prefixes, suffixes, and one nickname if reasonable alongside their appropriately designated name. No flat-out copying characters from popular media. A reference is okay, but give it enough variance to not be a straight up copycat character.
Admins may ask you to change your name at any point if it's low-effort / overdone (John Central Command).
## Act and behave within the spirit of the Job you have been assigned.
Security and Command Are Held to Higher Standards. Security and Command players have a vital role in the round and are thus expected to know the basic mechanics of the game, the areas of their departments, and knowledge of Space Law and their respective SOPs.
If you must leave as a member of Command, inform the rest of Command and head to Cryo. If you don't have time for this, leave a quick Ahelp.
If you are temporarily role banned for failing to do either of these (ex: an emergency that didn't give you time), you can message the admins to revert the role ban upon returning.
Security is expected toward violence as a corporate boot and working in favor of Nanotrasen and not the common-folk.
Command being expected to be self-interested rather than benevolent.
Consistent gross-abuse of the authority Security and/or Command has will result in a role ban or regular ban if you go outside the scope of Play Your Character.
## Play Animals Realistically
Animals should be played with some semblance of realism to respect the immersion of other players. This includes:
[bullet] Not reporting antags to security
[bullet] Not asking for cognizine
[bullet] Using emotes to bypass speech limitations
[bullet] Playing "antag" animals and destroying chems, welderbombing, or loosing. (You can eat paper, however)
[bullet] Players should not allow station pets, Pun-Pun, and Yip-Yap to become heads of staff nor ask to become such. Pun-Pun and Yip-Yap should also not be employed outside of their service work.
## Shiva
Shiva's role is to be that of the security's attack dog. Shiva should not be seeking out antagonists (valid hunting), but can defend the station/crew when reasonable. She should focus on protection over chasing down antags unless specifically told to by HOS. Shiva cannot recognize specific antag objects without reason (ie. Not knowing what a Heretic circle is, but recognizing what a gun is).
## Cogni'd Xeno's and Dragons
All Xeno's and Dragons are considered antags, even when given cognizine. You should not suddenly become friendly to the player(s) who gave you cogni.
You should still commit to your roles as an antag. You can be deceptive to befriend someone via manipulation, but you should still be killing/eating them eventually.
## No End-Of-Round Griefing (EORG)
End-of-Round Grief (EORG) is classified, generally, as being needlessly violent or acting out-of-character once the round has ended (designated by the end of round screen pop-up), to the detriment of other players' enjoyment or immersion.
You are expected to continue to roleplay as you had for the rest of the round, including on the shuttle to CC. You should not suddenly break character to cause chaos just because round has ended or near ending.
EORG is mirrored for crew left on the station. However, you should not be willingly staying behind and should attempt to go to CC as crew.
Examples of unallowed actions:
[bullet] Destroying all the lights because it's funny
[bullet] Killing someone because they offended you
[bullet] Breaking into cargo to get loot
[bullet] Shooting your PKA at walls "just because"
Examples of allowed actions:
[bullet] Punching the bartender because you have been feuding all shift
[bullet] Arresting someone who is wanted or causing trouble as security
[bullet] Pranking harmlessly as the clown
